claim: The Cohesin complex prevents premature differentiation of Drosophila ISCs into enterocytes (ECs).
source: The Cohesin complex regulates transcription globally by generating topologically-associated DNA domains (TADs) that link promotor regions with distant enhancers. We show here that the Cohesin complex prevents premature differentiation of Drosophila ISCs into enterocytes (ECs).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1-2.

claim: Depletion of the Cohesin subunit Rad21 triggers an ISC to EC differentiation program that is independent of Notch signaling.
source: Depletion of the Cohesin subunit Rad21 and the loading factor Nipped-B triggers an ISC to EC differentiation program that is independent of Notch signaling, but can be rescued by over-expression of the ISC-specific escargot (esg) transcription factor.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data in Figure 8 showing differentiation occurs even when Notch is knocked down.

claim: Depletion of the loading factor Nipped-B triggers an ISC to EC differentiation program that is independent of Notch signaling.
source: Depletion of the Cohesin subunit Rad21 and the loading factor Nipped-B triggers an ISC to EC differentiation program that is independent of Notch signaling, but can be rescued by over-expression of the ISC-specific escargot (esg) transcription factor.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: Over-expression of the ISC-specific escargot (esg) transcription factor can rescue the ISC to EC differentiation program triggered by Rad21 depletion.
source: Depletion of the Cohesin subunit Rad21 and the loading factor Nipped-B triggers an ISC to EC differentiation program that is independent of Notch signaling, but can be rescued by over-expression of the ISC-specific escargot (esg) transcription factor.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data in Figure 9.

claim: Cohesin regulates Esg binding to promoters of differentiation genes.
source: Using damID and transcriptomic analysis, we find that Cohesin regulates Esg binding to promoters of differentiation genes, including a group of Notch target genes involved in ISC differentiation.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by damID data in Figure 6H-K.

claim: Cohesin regulates Esg binding to promoters of Notch target genes involved in ISC differentiation.
source: Using damID and transcriptomic analysis, we find that Cohesin regulates Esg binding to promoters of differentiation genes, including a group of Notch target genes involved in ISC differentiation.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by damID data in Figure 6J.

claim: Cohesin ensures efficient Esg-dependent gene repression to maintain stemness and intestinal homeostasis.
source: We propose that Cohesin ensures efficient Esg-dependent gene repression to maintain stemness and intestinal homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: ISCs contribute to epithelial homeostasis in the gastrointestinal tract due to their capacity to proliferate and renew old or damaged tissue.
source: Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) contribute to epithelial homeostasis in the gastrointestinal tract due to their capacity to proliferate and renew old or damaged tissue (Casali and Batlle, 2009; Biteau et al., 2011; Signer and Morrison, 2013; Barker, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: ISCs self-renew and supply cells that differentiate into different lineages needed to perform all essential functions of the intestinal epithelium.
source: ISCs self-renew and supply cells that differentiate into different lineages needed to perform all essential functions of the intestinal epithelium (Jiang and Edgar, 2011; Li and Jasper, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: ISC maintenance and proliferative activity influences intestinal homeostasis, as well as the general fitness and healthy life span (or healthspan) of the organism.
source: ISC maintenance and proliferative activity thus influences intestinal homeostasis, as well as the general fitness and healthy life span (or healthspan) of the organism (Li and Jasper, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The intestinal epithelium in the fly midgut consists of ISCs, enteroblasts (EBs), enterocytes (ECs) and enteroendocrine (EEs) cells.
source: The intestinal epithelium in the fly midgut consists of ISCs, enteroblasts (EBs), enterocytes (ECs) and enteroendocrine (EEs) cells (Miguel-Aliaga et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: ISCs are the main mitotic cells in the Drosophila midgut tissue.
source: ISCs are the main mitotic cells in this tissue and can give rise to all cell types performing essential secretory, absorptive and immune roles (Ayyaz and Jasper, 2013; Li and Jasper, 2016; Liu and Jin, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: ISCs can give rise to all cell types performing essential secretory, absorptive and immune roles in the Drosophila midgut.
source: ISCs are the main mitotic cells in this tissue and can give rise to all cell types performing essential secretory, absorptive and immune roles (Ayyaz and Jasper, 2013; Li and Jasper, 2016; Liu and Jin, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Infection or stress triggers ISC proliferation through the activation of JAK/STAT, JNK, and EGFR signaling pathways.
source: Infection or stress, for example, triggers ISC proliferation through the activation of JAK/STAT, JNK, and EGFR signaling pathways (Biteau et al., 2008; Jiang and Edgar, 2009; Jiang et al., 2009; Buchon et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2010; Jiang et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Notch activity limits ISC proliferation.
source: Notch activity limits ISC proliferation and is required for EB differentiation into ECs (Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007; Kapuria et al., 2012; Guo and Ohlstein, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Notch activity is required for EB differentiation into ECs.
source: Notch activity limits ISC proliferation and is required for EB differentiation into ECs (Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007; Kapuria et al., 2012; Guo and Ohlstein, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Escargot (Esg) positively regulates expression of stemness genes.
source: Intrinsic regulators of ISC maintenance include the master transcription factor Escargot (Esg), which positively regulates expression of stemness genes, but inhibits expression of differentiation factors, including of the transcription factor Nubbin/Pdm1 (Korzelius et al., 2014; Loza-Coll et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Escargot (Esg) inhibits expression of differentiation factors, including the transcription factor Nubbin/Pdm1.
source: Intrinsic regulators of ISC maintenance include the master transcription factor Escargot (Esg), which positively regulates expression of stemness genes, but inhibits expression of differentiation factors, including of the transcription factor Nubbin/Pdm1 (Korzelius et al., 2014; Loza-Coll et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin is a ring-like structure formed by a complex of proteins (Smc1, Smc3, Rad21 and SA1/SA2 proteins) that interact with DNA.
source: Cohesin, a ring-like structure formed by a complex of proteins (Smc1, Smc3, Rad21 and SA1/SA2 proteins) that interact with DNA, is a key element in genome organization (Peters et al., 2008; Feeney et al., 2010; Singh and Gerton, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin is a key element in genome organization.
source: Cohesin, a ring-like structure formed by a complex of proteins (Smc1, Smc3, Rad21 and SA1/SA2 proteins) that interact with DNA, is a key element in genome organization (Peters et al., 2008; Feeney et al., 2010; Singh and Gerton, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: During mitosis, Cohesin encircles paired chromosomes and holds them together until late anaphase.
source: During mitosis, Cohesin encircles paired chromosomes and holds them together until late anaphase, when Rad21 is cleaved by the protease Separase to allow chromosome segregation towards centrosomes (Haarhuis et al., 2014; Morales and Losada, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Rad21 is cleaved by the protease Separase during late anaphase to allow chromosome segregation towards centrosomes.
source: During mitosis, Cohesin encircles paired chromosomes and holds them together until late anaphase, when Rad21 is cleaved by the protease Separase to allow chromosome segregation towards centrosomes (Haarhuis et al., 2014; Morales and Losada, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Up to 13% of Cohesin has been reported to be sufficient for chromosome cohesion.
source: While only a minor amount (up to 13%) of Cohesin has been reported to be sufficient for chromosome cohesion (Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2010) most of Cohesin appears to be involved in chromatin organization in interphase cells via organization of topologically-associated domains (TADs) by means of loop extrusion (Dekker and Mirny, 2016; Rao et al., 2017; Wutz et al., 2017; Yuen and Gerton, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Most of Cohesin appears to be involved in chromatin organization in interphase cells via organization of topologically-associated domains (TADs) by means of loop extrusion.
source: While only a minor amount (up to 13%) of Cohesin has been reported to be sufficient for chromosome cohesion (Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2010) most of Cohesin appears to be involved in chromatin organization in interphase cells via organization of topologically-associated domains (TADs) by means of loop extrusion (Dekker and Mirny, 2016; Rao et al., 2017; Wutz et al., 2017; Yuen and Gerton, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Within TADs, Cohesin interacts with transcription factors and brings promotors into proximity with enhancers.
source: Within TADs, Cohesin interacts with transcription factors and brings promotors into proximity with enhancers (Schaaf et al., 2013; Merkenschlager and Nora, 2016; Novo et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin deficiency results in the elimination of TADs and alters transcription.
source: Cohesin deficiency results in the elimination of TADs and alters transcription, supporting its crucial function in gene expression (Pauli et al., 2010; Dorsett and Ström, 2012; Zuin et al., 2014; Lupiáñez et al., 2015; Rao et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin deficiency has been shown to cause prominent changes in genomic organization, leading to transcription being dependent on local transcriptional elements and cryptic promotors rather than on distant enhancer elements.
source: Cohesin deficiency has further been shown to cause prominent changes in genomic organization, leading to transcription being dependent on local transcriptional elements and cryptic promotors rather than on distant enhancer elements (Schwarzer et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Knock down of Rad21 using esg-FlpOut system resulted in clones mostly containing individual cells with large nuclei and expressing Pdm1.
source: Using this system, knock down of Rad21 (using two independent shRNA constructs targeting Rad21) resulted in clones mostly containing individual cells with large nuclei and expressing Pdm1, indicating that Rad21 knock down triggered ISC differentiation into enterocytes (ECs) (Lee et al., 2009; Beebe et al., 2010; Mathur et al., 2010; Korzelius et al., 2014) (Figure 1A and B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Rad21 knock down triggered ISC differentiation into enterocytes (ECs).
source: Using this system, knock down of Rad21 (using two independent shRNA constructs targeting Rad21) resulted in clones mostly containing individual cells with large nuclei and expressing Pdm1, indicating that Rad21 knock down triggered ISC differentiation into enterocytes (ECs) (Lee et al., 2009; Beebe et al., 2010; Mathur et al., 2010; Korzelius et al., 2014) (Figure 1A and B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1A and B, with additional support from citations.

claim: Rad21-deficient cells became larger than wild-type ISCs.
source: Rad21-deficient cells became larger (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and their nuclei were significantly bigger than nuclei of WT ISCs, supporting the notion of their terminal differentiation into ECs (Figure 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Nuclei of Rad21-deficient cells were significantly bigger than nuclei of WT ISCs.
source: Rad21-deficient cells became larger (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and their nuclei were significantly bigger than nuclei of WT ISCs, supporting the notion of their terminal differentiation into ECs (Figure 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cohesin-depleted clones showed a significant increase in Pdm1 positive cells.
source: While Cohesin-depleted clones showed a significant increase in Pdm1 positive cells (Figure 1), they were not in fact smaller with respect to the numbers of cells per clone.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Cohesin-depleted clones were not smaller with respect to the numbers of cells per clone compared to wild-type clones.
source: While Cohesin-depleted clones showed a significant increase in Pdm1 positive cells (Figure 1), they were not in fact smaller with respect to the numbers of cells per clone. Their size was about equal compared to wild-type clones, with some minor variability in the exact number of cells seen in different guts (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Loss of Rad21 inhibited ISC proliferation in response to infection by Erwinia carotovora carotovora 15 (Ecc15).
source: Consistent with ectopic ISC differentiation, loss of Rad21 inhibited ISC proliferation in response to infection by the mild enteropathogen Erwinia carotovora carotovora 15 (Ecc15), as assessed by the quantification of phospho-Histone H3+ cells in the gut (Figure 1D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Rad21 is loaded onto chromosomes by the kollerin complex, which includes Nipped-B.
source: Rad21/Cohesin is loaded onto chromosomes by the kollerin complex, which includes Nipped-B, and on chromosome arms is removed during mitotic prophase by Polo kinase, likely via phosphorylation of its SA1/SA2 subunits, while the centromeric pool of Cohesin is removed during the metaphase to anaphase transition by Separase (Hauf et al., 2005; Dorsett, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: On chromosome arms, Rad21/Cohesin is removed during mitotic prophase by Polo kinase, likely via phosphorylation of its SA1/SA2 subunits.
source: Rad21/Cohesin is loaded onto chromosomes by the kollerin complex, which includes Nipped-B, and on chromosome arms is removed during mitotic prophase by Polo kinase, likely via phosphorylation of its SA1/SA2 subunits, while the centromeric pool of Cohesin is removed during the metaphase to anaphase transition by Separase (Hauf et al., 2005; Dorsett, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The centromeric pool of Cohesin is removed during the metaphase to anaphase transition by Separase.
source: Rad21/Cohesin is loaded onto chromosomes by the kollerin complex, which includes Nipped-B, and on chromosome arms is removed during mitotic prophase by Polo kinase, likely via phosphorylation of its SA1/SA2 subunits, while the centromeric pool of Cohesin is removed during the metaphase to anaphase transition by Separase (Hauf et al., 2005; Dorsett, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Knock down of Nipped-B induced premature ISC differentiation, indicated by ectopic Pdm1 expression.
source: Similar to reducing rad21 expression, these perturbations induced premature ISC differentiation, indicated by ectopic Pdm1 expression (Figure 2A–C) and inhibition of mitotic activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Over-expression of constitutively active Polo mutant poloT182D induced premature ISC differentiation, indicated by ectopic Pdm1 expression.
source: Similar to reducing rad21 expression, these perturbations induced premature ISC differentiation, indicated by ectopic Pdm1 expression (Figure 2A–C) and inhibition of mitotic activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Depletion of CTCF did not trigger ISC differentiation.
source: Interestingly, depletion of the chromatin-shaping and transcriptional repressor and insulator CTCF (CCCTC-binding factor) (Sexton and Cavalli, 2015) did not trigger ISC differentiation (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Loading of Rad21/Cohesin onto chromatin is crucial for ISC maintenance and to prevent premature differentiation of ISCs.
source: These data suggest that loading of Rad21/Cohesin onto chromatin is crucial for ISC maintenance and to prevent premature differentiation of ISCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing effects of Nipped-B knockdown and Polo activation.

claim: ISCs divide at a very low rate in homeostatic conditions.
source: It is important to emphasize that ISCs divide at a very low rate in homeostatic conditions (Figures 1–4).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figures 1-4.

claim: In control flies, ISCs have for the most part not divided (single labeled cells) or divided only once (doublets) in the course of the experiments using esg-FlpOut system.
source: As shown in Figures 1A and 2A, in control flies, ISCs have for the most part, not divided (single labeled cells) or divided only once (doublets) in the course of the experiments.
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 1A and 2A.

claim: Rad21 knockdown, Polo activation, or NippedB knockdown resulted in cell differentiation regardless of whether ISCs had divided or not.
source: Rad21 knockdown, Polo activation, or NippedB knockdown resulted in cell differentiation regardless of whether ISCs had divided (clones with more than one labeled cell), or not (single labeled cell).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text based on analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Over-expression of Rad21-HA in ISCs using esg::Gal4 was sufficient to induce ISC proliferation in homeostatic conditions.
source: Over-expression of Rad21-HA in ISCs using esg::Gal4 was sufficient to induce ISC proliferation in homeostatic conditions, suggesting that Rad21 can act in ISCs, at least in part, independently of chromatid cohesion (Figure 3A and B; over-expressed Rad21-HA localized to the nucleus, Figure 3C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Rad21 can act in ISCs, at least in part, independently of chromatid cohesion.
source: Over-expression of Rad21-HA in ISCs using esg::Gal4 was sufficient to induce ISC proliferation in homeostatic conditions, suggesting that Rad21 can act in ISCs, at least in part, independently of chromatid cohesion (Figure 3A and B; over-expressed Rad21-HA localized to the nucleus, Figure 3C).
evidence: This is suggested based on the observation that Rad21 overexpression induces proliferation in homeostatic conditions.

claim: Rad21-HA overexpression in ISCs using esg-FlpOut system induced drastic cell overproliferation with formation of Pdm1-positive ECs.
source: Similarly, Rad21-HA overexpression in ISCs using esg-FlpOut system induced drastic cell overproliferation with formation of Pdm1-positive ECs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Rad21 influences ISC function via transcriptional regulation of proliferation and stemness genes in interphase.
source: We therefore hypothesized that Rad21 influences ISC function via transcriptional regulation of proliferation and stemness genes in interphase, similar to its role in the mammalian epidermis (Noutsou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the experimental observations and comparison to prior literature.

claim: Aneuploidy has been reported to cause ISC differentiation.
source: Aneuploidy has recently been reported to cause ISC differentiation (Gogendeau et al., 2015) and also to promote dysplasia (Resende et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Aneuploidy has been reported to promote dysplasia.
source: Aneuploidy has recently been reported to cause ISC differentiation (Gogendeau et al., 2015) and also to promote dysplasia (Resende et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Depletion of bub3 was found to induce ISC differentiation and thus loss of ISCs.
source: While depletion of bub3 was found to induce ISC differentiation and thus loss of ISCs (Gogendeau et al., 2015), depletion of BubR1, mad2, or mps1 all resulted in increased ISC proliferation and an accumulation of ISCs/EBs and EEs in the intestinal epithelium (Resende et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Depletion of BubR1, mad2, or mps1 all resulted in increased ISC proliferation and an accumulation of ISCs/EBs and EEs in the intestinal epithelium.
source: While depletion of bub3 was found to induce ISC differentiation and thus loss of ISCs (Gogendeau et al., 2015), depletion of BubR1, mad2, or mps1 all resulted in increased ISC proliferation and an accumulation of ISCs/EBs and EEs in the intestinal epithelium (Resende et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The differentiation response to Bub3 depletion seems to be a consequence of another function of Bub3, rather than the aneuploidy itself.
source: Since depletion of all four factors results in aneuploidy, the differentiation response to Bub3 depletion seems to be a consequence of another function of Bub3, rather than the aneuploidy itself.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the effects of different aneuploidy-inducing perturbations.

claim: Knock down of Cdk1, polo and aurora B caused premature ISC differentiation, indicated by ectopic Pdm1 and inhibited mitotic activity.
source: We knocked down the essential mitosis regulators Cdk1, polo and aurora B (Godinho and Tavares, 2008) using esgF/O, and monitored ISC differentiation and proliferation. These perturbations caused premature ISC differentiation, indicated by ectopic Pdm1 and inhibited mitotic activity (Figure 4A–C) reminiscent of results in published reports in which the checkpoint kinase Bub3 was knocked down (Gogendeau et al., 2015).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: The frequency of Pdm1-positive cells after Cdk1, polo and aurora B perturbations was prominently lower compared to downregulation of Rad21.
source: However, the frequency of Pdm1-positive cells after these perturbations (Figure 4B) was prominently lower compared to downregulation of Rad21 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This comparison is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 4B and 1B.

claim: AurB RNAi led to a significant reduction in Delta-lacZ expression.
source: AurB RNAi led to a significant reduction in Delta-lacZ expression, but Rad21 knock down completely eliminated this expression, indicating a more complete loss of stemness following Rad21 depletion than in other aneuploidy-inducing conditions (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Rad21 knock down completely eliminated Delta-lacZ expression.
source: AurB RNAi led to a significant reduction in Delta-lacZ expression, but Rad21 knock down completely eliminated this expression, indicating a more complete loss of stemness following Rad21 depletion than in other aneuploidy-inducing conditions (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Rad21 depletion results in a more complete loss of stemness than other aneuploidy-inducing conditions.
source: AurB RNAi led to a significant reduction in Delta-lacZ expression, but Rad21 knock down completely eliminated this expression, indicating a more complete loss of stemness following Rad21 depletion than in other aneuploidy-inducing conditions (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the Delta-lacZ expression data.

claim: Rad21 expression was significantly decreased in poloT182D–expressing ISCs compared to WT controls.
source: Finally, we compared Rad21 localization and expression between ISCs with deregulated mitosis (expressing poloT182D) and WT cells. Even though Rad21 was localized to the nucleus (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) its expression was significantly decreased in poloT182D–expressing ISCs compared to WT controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cell cycle defects could lead to Rad21 downregulation further triggering ISC differentiation.
source: Thus, cell cycle defects could lead to Rad21 downregulation further triggering ISC differentiation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that Polo activation reduces Rad21 expression.

claim: Rad21 knock down resulted in significant changes (q < 0.05 and Log2 equals or more then 1) in 985 genes.
source: Our data confirmed Rad21 knock down and overexpression, respectively, in ISCs (Figure 6E). We further observed that rad21 knockdown resulted in significant changes (q < 0.05 and Log2 equals or more then 1) in 985 genes against 489 genes in UAS-Rad21-HA samples (q < 0.05) with 160-gene overlap between conditions (Figure 6A and B, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by RNAseq data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Rad21 overexpression resulted in significant changes (q < 0.05) in 489 genes.
source: Our data confirmed Rad21 knock down and overexpression, respectively, in ISCs (Figure 6E). We further observed that rad21 knockdown resulted in significant changes (q < 0.05 and Log2 equals or more then 1) in 985 genes against 489 genes in UAS-Rad21-HA samples (q < 0.05) with 160-gene overlap between conditions (Figure 6A and B, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by RNAseq data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: There was a 160-gene overlap between Rad21 knockdown and overexpression conditions.
source: Our data confirmed Rad21 knock down and overexpression, respectively, in ISCs (Figure 6E). We further observed that rad21 knockdown resulted in significant changes (q < 0.05 and Log2 equals or more then 1) in 985 genes against 489 genes in UAS-Rad21-HA samples (q < 0.05) with 160-gene overlap between conditions (Figure 6A and B, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by RNAseq data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Approximately 8.6% (32) of genes upregulated in Rad21 RNAi were also induced when the transcriptional repressor Esg was knocked down.
source: Approximately 8,6% (32) of genes upregulated in Rad21 RNAi were also induced when the transcriptional repressor Esg was knocked down (Figure 6D and F), Figure 6—source data 1), including the transcription factor nubbin/pdm1, known to be repressed by Esg (Korzelius et al., 2014).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6D and F.

claim: EC-specific genes including Jon and trypsin family proteases, and ser6, were enriched (approximately 17%, 65 genes) after Rad21 knock down.
source: EC-specific genes including Jon and trypsin family proteases, and ser6, were also enriched (approximately 17%, 65 genes) after Rad21 knock down (Dutta et al., 2015; Doupé et al., 2018) (Figure 6C and G, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6C and G.

claim: Cell death markers were not upregulated after Rad21 knock down or over-expression.
source: Note that we did not observe upregulation of cell death markers after Rad21 knock down or over-expression (Figure 6, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by RNAseq data.

claim: Rad21 may be required for Esg-mediated repression of differentiation genes.
source: These results were consistent with the differentiation phenotype of rad21-deficient ISCs (Figure 1), and led us to hypothesize that Rad21 may be required for Esg-mediated repression of differentiation genes.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the transcriptomic data.

claim: Using damID, 1034 significant peaks were observed in esg-dam control samples.
source: Using a previously described esg-dam construct, we observed 1034 significant peaks in esg-dam control samples, 862 of which were not observed in rad21 deficient ISCs, indicating that the vast majority of DNA interactions of esg in ISCs depend on functional rad21 (Figure 6H Figure 7 and Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by damID data shown in Figure 6H and Figure 7.

claim: 862 of the esg-dam peaks were not observed in rad21 deficient ISCs.
source: Using a previously described esg-dam construct, we observed 1034 significant peaks in esg-dam control samples, 862 of which were not observed in rad21 deficient ISCs, indicating that the vast majority of DNA interactions of esg in ISCs depend on functional rad21 (Figure 6H Figure 7 and Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by damID data shown in Figure 6H and Figure 7.

claim: The vast majority of DNA interactions of esg in ISCs depend on functional rad21.
source: Using a previously described esg-dam construct, we observed 1034 significant peaks in esg-dam control samples, 862 of which were not observed in rad21 deficient ISCs, indicating that the vast majority of DNA interactions of esg in ISCs depend on functional rad21 (Figure 6H Figure 7 and Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the damID data.

claim: The lost esg interaction sites in rad21-deficient ISCs included locations close to differentiation and EC specific genes, such as nubbin/pdm1.
source: GO analysis of peaks appearing in Esg-Dam in contrast to Esg-Dam/Rad21 RNAi yielded a number of genes involved in ISC maintenance and differentiation pathways (Figure 6I and J) anticipated due to the function of esg, the lost interaction sites included locations close to differentiation and EC specific genes, such as nubbin/pdm1 (Figure 6K and Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by damID data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: Pdm1 was strongly induced after Rad21 downregulation as assessed by qRT-PCR on FACS-purified ISCs.
source: Finally, to verify our transcriptome data we performed qRT-PCR on FACS-purified Rad21-depleted ISCs and compared those to controls. We assessed expression of Pdm1 and esg, and found that, consistent with immunofluorescence data, Pdm1 was strongly induced after Rad21 downregulation, while Esg mRNA levels did not change after Rad21 knock down (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Esg mRNA levels did not change after Rad21 knock down as assessed by qRT-PCR on FACS-purified ISCs.
source: Finally, to verify our transcriptome data we performed qRT-PCR on FACS-purified Rad21-depleted ISCs and compared those to controls. We assessed expression of Pdm1 and esg, and found that, consistent with immunofluorescence data, Pdm1 was strongly induced after Rad21 downregulation, while Esg mRNA levels did not change after Rad21 knock down (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: When Rad21 was knocked down in Notch-deficient ISCs, these cells still differentiated into Pdm1-positive cells.
source: Loss of Notch in the ISC lineage perturbs differentiation, resulting in the formation of tumors consisting of ISCs and EEs. However, when Rad21 was knocked down in Notch-deficient ISCs, these cells still differentiated into Pdm1-positive cells (Figure 8A and B), and drastically inhibited ISC proliferation was observed (Figure 8C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: ISC differentiation induced by loss of Rad21 is independent of Notch signaling.
source: ISC differentiation induced by loss of Rad21 is thus independent of Notch signaling.
evidence: This conclusion is stated based on the observation that Rad21 knockdown causes differentiation even in Notch-deficient cells.

claim: Esg overexpression robustly inhibited ISC differentiation in Rad21 loss of function conditions, significantly reducing the number of Pdm1-positive cells.
source: Esg overexpression robustly inhibited ISC differentiation in these conditions, significantly reducing the number of Pdm1-positive cells and increasing the frequency of mitotic ISCs in homeostatic as well as regenerative conditions (after infection) (Figure 9).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Esg overexpression increased the frequency of mitotic ISCs in homeostatic as well as regenerative conditions in Rad21 loss of function conditions.
source: Esg overexpression robustly inhibited ISC differentiation in these conditions, significantly reducing the number of Pdm1-positive cells and increasing the frequency of mitotic ISCs in homeostatic as well as regenerative conditions (after infection) (Figure 9).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Rad21 plays a critical role in the Esg-mediated maintenance of the stem cell state in the ISC lineage.
source: These results indicate that Rad21 plays a critical role in the Esg-mediated maintenance of the stem cell state in the ISC lineage (Figure 10).
evidence: This conclusion is stated based on the rescue experiments with Esg overexpression.

claim: The requirement for Rad21 can be overcome by elevating Esg expression levels.
source: At the same time, however, these data indicate that the requirement for Rad21 can be overcome by elevating Esg expression levels, suggesting that Rad21 plays mostly an accessory role to ensure robust Esg-mediated gene regulation.
evidence: This conclusion is stated based on the observation that Esg overexpression rescues Rad21 knockdown phenotypes.

claim: Rad21 plays mostly an accessory role to ensure robust Esg-mediated gene regulation.
source: At the same time, however, these data indicate that the requirement for Rad21 can be overcome by elevating Esg expression levels, suggesting that Rad21 plays mostly an accessory role to ensure robust Esg-mediated gene regulation.
evidence: This is suggested based on the rescue of Rad21 knockdown by Esg overexpression.

claim: Cohesin depletion increases differentiation of skin stem cells.
source: At the same time, these studies highlight the selectivity and cell-type specificity of Cohesin function in different stem cell lineages: Cohesin depletion increases differentiation of skin stem cells, but inhibits hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) differentiation (Mullenders et al., 2015; Galeev et al., 2016; Noutsou et al., 2017; Cuartero et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin depletion inhibits hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) differentiation.
source: At the same time, these studies highlight the selectivity and cell-type specificity of Cohesin function in different stem cell lineages: Cohesin depletion increases differentiation of skin stem cells, but inhibits hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) differentiation (Mullenders et al., 2015; Galeev et al., 2016; Noutsou et al., 2017; Cuartero et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In HSCs, Cohesin mediates recruitment of the transcription factor NFκB to chromatin and induces immune and pro-survival gene expression.
source: In HSCs, Cohesin mediates recruitment of the transcription factor NFκB to chromatin and induces immune and pro-survival gene expression (Mullenders et al., 2015; Galeev et al., 2016; Cuartero et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin controls chromatin accessibility and activity of ERG, GATA2 and RUNX1 transcription factors in HSCs.
source: It has further been reported to control chromatin accessibility and activity of ERG, GATA2 and RUNX1 transcription factors in HSCs (Mazumdar et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: During hematopoiesis, the Polycomb protein ASLX1 interacts with Cohesin to maintain chromatid separation and transcription.
source: During hematopoiesis, the Polycomb protein ASLX1 interacts with Cohesin to maintain chromatid separation and transcription (Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: By mediating recruitment and transcriptional activity of the pluripotency factors Klf4, Esrrb and Sox2, Cohesin regulates pluripotency of embryonic stem cells.
source: By mediating recruitment and transcriptional activity of the pluripotency factors Klf4, Esrrb and Sox2, Cohesin also regulates pluripotency of embryonic stem cells (Nitzsche et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Elevated Rad21 expression has been implicated in loss of heterozygosity at the APC locus in the mammalian intestine.
source: In the mammalian intestine, elevated Rad21 expression has been implicated in loss of heterozygosity at the APC locus, as well as the activation of L1 retrotransposons (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Elevated Rad21 expression has been implicated in the activation of L1 retrotransposons in the mammalian intestine.
source: In the mammalian intestine, elevated Rad21 expression has been implicated in loss of heterozygosity at the APC locus, as well as the activation of L1 retrotransposons (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin supports Esg function by facilitating access of the transcription factor to promotor regions of differentiation genes.
source: We propose that Cohesin supports Esg function by facilitating access of the transcription factor to promotor regions of differentiation genes, and that in the absence of cohesion, chromatin organization is relaxed, allowing ectopic expression of differentiation genes (Figure 10).
evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: In the absence of cohesin, chromatin organization is relaxed, allowing ectopic expression of differentiation genes.
source: We propose that Cohesin supports Esg function by facilitating access of the transcription factor to promotor regions of differentiation genes, and that in the absence of cohesion, chromatin organization is relaxed, allowing ectopic expression of differentiation genes (Figure 10).
evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: By providing excess Esg protein, differentiation gene promoters can be repressed even in the absence of Rad21.
source: By providing excess Esg protein, such promoters can then be repressed even in the absence of Rad21.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the rescue of Rad21 knockdown by Esg overexpression.

claim: Cohesin has been shown to regulate gene expression via interaction with the Mediator complex of Polymerase II.
source: Mechanistically, how may Cohesin regulate Esg-mediated gene expression? In other systems, Cohesin has been shown to regulate gene expression via interaction with the Mediator complex of Polymerase II (Kagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Depletion of Mediator subunits in ISCs can cause premature differentiation.
source: Such a function of Cohesin in the transcriptional regulation complex of Esg is supported by the fact that depletion of Mediator subunits in ISCs can cause premature differentiation (Zeng et al., 2015), reminiscent of the Cohesin loss of function phenotype.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Loss of Cohesin results in ISC differentiation independently of aneuploidy.
source: Based on our findings and our observations, we propose that loss of Cohesin results in ISC differentiation independently of aneuploidy for a number of reasons:
evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both depleting Cohesin as well as promoting its release from DNA induces ISC differentiation.
source: First, we find that both depleting Cohesin as well as promoting its release from DNA induces ISC differentiation.
evidence: This observation is stated as evidence for aneuploidy-independent effects.

claim: The various perturbations to Cohesin (two independent Rad21 shRNAs, Nipped B shRNA, T182D Polo mutant) elicited a significantly stronger differentiation phenotype compared to perturbations of other regulators of mitosis (AurB, Cdk1, Polo).
source: The various perturbations to that effect (two independent Rad21 shRNAs, Nipped B shRNA, T182D Polo mutant) elicited a significantly stronger differentiation phenotype compared to perturbations of other regulators of mitosis (AurB, Cdk1, Polo), indicating that the mitotic role of Cohesin could not completely account for the observed robust differentiation of ISCs into ECs (Figure 1, Figure 2 and Figure 3).
evidence: This comparison is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 1, 2, and 3.

claim: All Cohesin and mitosis perturbations resulted in a complete inhibition of proliferation, indicating a comparable level of cell cycle arrest.
source: Importantly, all of these perturbations resulted in a complete inhibition of proliferation, indicating a comparable level of cell cycle arrest (Figure 1D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The binding of Cohesin to chromatin after completion of mitosis is mediated in interphase by the complex containing Nipped B.
source: Second, the fact that Nipped B knockdown also results in ISC differentiation strongly supports an aneuploidy-independent mechanism, as the binding of Cohesin to chromatin after completion of mitosis is mediated in interphase by the complex containing Nipped B.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about Cohesin loading.

claim: Cohesin binding to chromatin in interphase is critical for ISC maintenance.
source: These data thus suggest that Cohesin binding to chromatin in interphase is critical for ISC maintenance (Figure 2A and C).
evidence: This conclusion is stated based on the Nipped B knockdown data.

claim: ISCs enter mitosis at a very low rate (up to approximately 10–20%) in unchallenged young fly midguts.
source: Third, ISCs are normally quiescent in unchallenged young fly midguts and enter mitosis at a very low rate (up to approximately 10–20%) (Figure 1D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 3B and Figure 4C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Cohesin depletion led to differentiation of around 60–70% of all ISCs.
source: In contrast, Cohesin depletion led to differentiation of around 60–70% of all ISCs (Figure 1B), and to an almost complete elimination of Delta-positive cells (to approximately 2%) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figures 1B and 5B.

claim: Cohesin depletion led to an almost complete elimination of Delta-positive cells (to approximately 2%).
source: In contrast, Cohesin depletion led to differentiation of around 60–70% of all ISCs (Figure 1B), and to an almost complete elimination of Delta-positive cells (to approximately 2%) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The drastic effect of Cohesin depletion on ISC differentiation does not reflect the frequency of cells entering mitosis.
source: Such a drastic effect does not reflect the frequency of cells entering mitosis.
evidence: This is stated as an argument against aneuploidy being the primary cause of differentiation.

claim: Cohesin depletion led to loss of Esg promotor binding.
source: Accordingly, Cohesin depletion led to loss of Esg promotor binding, and significantly reduced Esg-regulated transcripts.
evidence: This observation is stated based on the damID and transcriptomic data.

claim: Cohesin depletion significantly reduced Esg-regulated transcripts.
source: Accordingly, Cohesin depletion led to loss of Esg promotor binding, and significantly reduced Esg-regulated transcripts.
evidence: This observation is stated based on the transcriptomic data.

claim: Esg over-expression in Cohesin-depleted cells significantly rescued the premature ISC differentiation.
source: Esg over-expression in Cohesin-depleted cells further significantly rescued the premature ISC differentiation (Figure 9) and restored homeostasis.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Esg over-expression in Cohesin-depleted cells restored homeostasis.
source: Esg over-expression in Cohesin-depleted cells further significantly rescued the premature ISC differentiation (Figure 9) and restored homeostasis.
evidence: This observation is stated based on the rescue experiments.

claim: It seems unlikely that the effects on Esg promoter loading and Esg-mediated gene regulation are merely an indirect consequence of aneuploidy.
source: It seems unlikely that these effects on Esg promoter loading and Esg-mediated gene regulation are merely an indirect consequence of aneuploidy.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Differentiation as a consequence of aneuploidy does not seem to be a robust phenotype.
source: It is important to point out further that differentiation as a consequence of aneuploidy does not seem to be a robust phenotype: While depletion of bub3 was found to induce ISC differentiation and thus loss of ISCs, depletion of BubR1, mad2, or mps1 all result in increased ISC proliferation and an accumulation of ISCs/EBs and EEs in the intestinal epithelium (Gogendeau et al., 2015; Resende et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation based on comparing results from different studies.

claim: Several recent studies on CTCF in Drosophila found little evidence of CTCF in chromosome domain/loop formation.
source: Several recent studies on CTCF in Drosophila found little evidence of CTCF in chromosome domain/loop formation (Ramírez et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2018; Matthews and White, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Other insulator protein complexes such as BEAF-32/CP190 or BEAF-32/Chromator have been implicated in TAD organization in Drosophila.
source: Other insulator protein complexes such as BEAF-32/CP190 or BEAF-32/Chromator have been implicated in TAD organization in Drosophila (Ramírez et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2018; Matthews and White, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Fly CTCF is not a major boundary definition protein but is rather a regulator of Hox or other gene expression.
source: Therefore, it has been recently proposed that fly CTCF is not a major boundary definition protein but is rather a regulator of Hox or other gene expression (Gambetta and Furlong, 2018; Szabo et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin has been suggested to maintain transcriptional memory after mitosis.
source: Cohesin has been suggested to maintain transcriptional memory after mitosis (Yan et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Some level of Cohesin has been detected in mitosis and suggested to mediate reloading of transcription factors onto DNA to resume gene expression in interphase.
source: Contrary to original observations of complete Cohesin removal, some level of Cohesin has been detected in mitosis and suggested to mediate reloading of transcription factors onto DNA to resume gene expression in interphase (Yan et al., 2013) or maintain gene expression in mitosis (Teves et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cohesin has been suggested to maintain gene expression in mitosis.
source: Contrary to original observations of complete Cohesin removal, some level of Cohesin has been detected in mitosis and suggested to mediate reloading of transcription factors onto DNA to resume gene expression in interphase (Yan et al., 2013) or maintain gene expression in mitosis (Teves et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: It is possible that Rad21 in ISCs ensures reloading of Esg onto relevant promoters after mitosis to maintain stable expression of stemness genes and ensure self-renewal.
source: Based on these reports and our data, it is possible that Rad21 in ISCs ensures reloading of Esg onto relevant promoters after mitosis to maintain stable expression of stemness genes and ensure self-renewal (Gogendeau et al., 2015) (Figure 10).
evidence: This is stated as a possibility based on prior literature and the current findings.

claim: Downregulation of mitotic factors and Rad21 release from chromatin leads to premature ISC differentiation.
source: Accordingly, we show that downregulation of mitotic factors and Rad21 release from chromatin leads to premature ISC differentiation.
evidence: This observation is stated based on the experimental data.

claim: Expression of constitutively active Polo, which is known to force cells into mitosis, remove Cohesin from chromatin, and extend the duration of mitosis, triggers drastic ISC differentiation.
source: Furthermore, expression of constitutively active Polo, which is known to force cells into mitosis (Sumara et al., 2002; van de Weerdt et al., 2005), remove Cohesin from chromatin, and extend the duration of mitosis, triggers drastic ISC differentiation.
evidence: This observation is stated based on the experimental data and prior literature.

claim: Recent evidence indicates that chromatin loops to a great extent could be reestablished shortly after Cohesin removal from chromatin.
source: Recent evidence indicates that chromatin loops to a great extent could be reestablished shortly after Cohesin removal from chromatin (Rao et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Acute Cohesin depletion slightly inhibits but nevertheless preserves cell proliferation of developing neuroblasts.
source: It is also interesting that acute Cohesin depletion slightly inhibits but nevertheless preserves cell proliferation of developing neuroblasts (Mirkovic et al., 2019) indicating a complex and still understudied role of Cohesin in mitosis, which may include cell type-, stage- or organism-dependent differences in mitosis, involve other cellular processes and non-cell autonomous mechanisms.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.
